newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal will meet EMU inflation goal - Bank chief.
newsitem.headline: Portugal will meet EMU inflation goal - Bank chief.

text.p: Portugal will meet the inflation criterion for entry to the single currency if the present trend is maintained, Bank of Portugal governor Antonio de Sousa said.
"If the present conditions are maintained, Portugal is going to fulfill the Maastricht Treaty in terms of inflation," de Sousa told journalists.

The European Union's Maastricht Treaty sets out the conditions that member countries must meet to gain access to monetary union, due to be launched in January 1999. It says the average rate of inflation, measured over a one year period, should not exceed by more than 1-1/2 percentage points that of, at most, the three best performing member states in terms of price stability.
Portugal's year-on-year inflation slowed to 2.5 percent in March from 2.9 percent in February.
